description: Product descriptive attributes (Colour, Size, Width cm, Height cm) surfaced through the API and admin UI, plus admin-editable product quantity backed by a product-level InventoryItem. Admin product create/edit sets the attributes and sets/updates the product-level InventoryItem QuantityOnHand + LowStockThreshold (creating one if absent); the admin list shows stock quantity; the product detail page shows the attributes. Depends on FEAT-001 (Product columns already added there); independent of FEAT-002/FEAT-003.
steps: ViewModels: add Colour/Size/Width/Height and int QuantityOnHand + int LowStockThreshold to ProductUpsertRequest (src/Shop.DAL/ViewModels/AdminProductViewModels.cs). Add Colour/Size/Width/Height to ProductDetailVM and (Colour/Size for display) to ProductListItemVM (src/Shop.DAL/ViewModels/CatalogViewModels.cs); add int QuantityOnHand to ProductDetailVM and ProductListItemVM for the admin list.

MappingProfile (src/Shop.Api/Mapping/MappingProfile.cs): Colour/Size/Width/Height map automatically by name on the Product->ProductDetailVM / Product->ProductListItemVM read maps (no change needed, but verify). For the QuantityOnHand admin-list value, map from the product-level inventory: on ProductDetailVM/ProductListItemVM map QuantityOnHand from s.InventoryItems.Where(i => i.VariantId == null).Sum(i => i.QuantityOnHand) (keep the existing TotalQuantityOnHand on ProductDetailVM as-is). The ProductUpsertRequest->Product write map already ignores InventoryItems; Colour/Size/Width/Height are client-editable scalars that map by name — no new ignores needed, but DO add explicit ignores if AssertConfigurationIsValid flags QuantityOnHand/LowStockThreshold as unmapped destination members (they are request-only inputs, not Product members, so they will not appear on the write map).

AdminProductsController (src/Shop.Api/Controllers/Admin/AdminProductsController.cs): in Create, after adding the product and Save (so the product has an Id), upsert a product-level InventoryItem — find product.InventoryItems.FirstOrDefault(i => i.VariantId == null); if none, Add a new InventoryItem { ProductId = product.Id, VariantId = null, QuantityOnHand = request.QuantityOnHand, LowStockThreshold = request.LowStockThreshold, IsDemoData = false } via _repo._InventoryItem; else update its QuantityOnHand/LowStockThreshold; then Save. In Update, load the product WITH .Include(p => p.InventoryItems), map the attribute fields, re-derive slug, then do the same product-level InventoryItem upsert. Leave variant-level inventory rows untouched. Return the ProductDetailVM re-queried with InventoryItems included so the response reflects the new quantity.

Frontend models (client/src/app/core/models/api.models.ts): add colour/size/width/height and quantityOnHand to ProductDetail and ProductListItem; (the admin uses loose any for products but the detail page is typed).

Admin product form (client/src/app/features/admin/admin-products/admin-products.component.ts + .html): add form fields for colour, size, width (cm), height (cm), quantityOnHand, lowStockThreshold; include them in blankForm(), startEdit() prefill, and the create/update payload. Add a Stock column to the product table showing p.quantityOnHand.
Product detail page (client/src/app/features/product-detail/product-detail.component.html): show the attributes (Colour, Size, Width cm, Height cm) when present, near the price/description.
acceptance_criteria: `dotnet build Shop.sln -c Debug` reports 0 errors (AutoMapper config still valid).

Against the running API with an admin JWT: creating a product with colour/size/width/height + quantity persists them, GET api/catalog/{id} returns the attributes, and the created product has a product-level InventoryItem with the given QuantityOnHand; editing the quantity updates that same InventoryItem (no duplicate rows).
The admin product list shows a stock quantity column and the product detail page shows the attributes.
verification: Runtime smoke: with the API running and an admin token, POST a new product with attributes + quantity, GET it back via api/admin/products and api/catalog/{id} to confirm attributes + stock; PUT a new quantity and confirm the same InventoryItem updated; then STOP the API.
findings: Implemented product descriptive attributes (Colour/Size/Width cm/Height cm) and admin-editable product-level quantity. Backend: added Colour/Size/Width/Height + QuantityOnHand/LowStockThreshold to ProductUpsertRequest; added Colour/Size/Width/Height + QuantityOnHand to ProductDetailVM and Colour/Size + QuantityOnHand to ProductListItemVM (TotalQuantityOnHand kept as-is). MappingProfile: attribute scalars map by name on the read maps; QuantityOnHand on both read maps maps from s.InventoryItems.Where(i => i.VariantId == null).Sum(i => i.QuantityOnHand); no new write-map ignores were needed because QuantityOnHand/LowStockThreshold are request-only inputs not present on Product, and Colour/Size/Width/Height map by name. AdminProductsController: Create saves the product then upserts a single product-level InventoryItem (VariantId == null) via _repo._InventoryItem; Update loads the product with .Include(p => p.InventoryItems), maps attributes, re-derives the slug, and upserts the same product-level row (create if absent, else update) leaving variant inventory untouched; both actions return a re-queried ProductDetailVM (helper GetDetailVM). Frontend: ProductDetail/ProductListItem models extended; admin product form gained colour/size/width(cm)/height(cm)/quantityOnHand/lowStockThreshold inputs wired through blankForm/startEdit/payload; added a Stock column to the admin product table; product-detail page shows the attributes near the price/description. Verification: `dotnet build Shop.sln -c Debug` = Build succeeded, 0 warnings, 0 errors; `npx ng build` from client/ = exit 0, bundle generated. Runtime smoke (API on SQLite demo DB, admin JWT): created product id=115 with colour=Crimson/size=Large/width=12.5/height=7.25/qty=30; GET api/catalog/115 returned the attributes and a product-level quantity of 30; PUT quantity=17 updated the SAME InventoryItem (re-GET returned quantityOnHand=17 and totalQuantityOnHand=17, confirming no duplicate inventory row). API stopped after verification. Note: the slug has a UNIQUE constraint, so creating a product whose name slugifies to an existing slug returns HTTP 500 from the DB (pre-existing behavior, unchanged by this feature).
